top_stories.title: Kava Lend Exploited for $3.8M via Market Manipulation
points: Attacker drained 55.2M KAVA tokens by exploiting a dormant BUSD market, shrinking its supply to near-zero to inflate deposit values ~243,000-fold.
Hacker borrowed KAVA against these inflated deposits 127 times, bridged ~49.2M KAVA to BNB Chain, and sold for roughly $2.1M.

Preparation began November 8; Kava paused the Axelar bridge (a cross-chain tool that lets assets move between different blockchains) and confirmed the exploit was contained to Kava Lend with no infinite minting issue.
KAVA token dropped ~39-40%; exchanges halted deposits and withdrawals in response.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum Slide Amid Broad Market Selloff
points: Bitcoin dropped to $42,500, its lowest price since July, as sentiment shifted away from risk assets amid broader economic uncertainty.
Ethereum fell 8% to $2,100 alongside Bitcoin's decline, with altcoins seeing similar downward pressure.
Trading volumes rose significantly during the selloff, indicating active liquidations of leveraged positions (trades amplified using borrowed funds) as prices fell.

items.title: Lawmaker Pushes to Ban Federal Employees From Prediction Market Betting
points: House Oversight Chair James Comer urges legislation banning federal employees from betting on prediction markets (platforms where users wager on real-world event outcomes).
Cited cases include Army soldiers and White House staff profiting from bets on election and political outcomes.

items.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI-Driven Shopping
points: ChatGPT Wallet lets an AI agent complete purchases on merchant sites using one-time substitute card numbers, so the agent never sees your real card data.
Users approve each purchase via Face ID; card networks cap the substitute number at the approved amount.
Users keep their points and dispute rights; issuers gain purchase visibility and merchants get lower interchange fees plus customer identity data.
Currently limited to US ChatGPT Pro users 18+ with Amex, Mastercard, or Visa, using vault technology and enrollment in Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay, and Amex ACE programs.
Friction points include per-purchase approval, partial card coverage, slow browser checkout, and many sites still blocking AI agents.

items.title: Traders Extract $6M+ From Public Data Ahead of Robinhood Listings
points: Traders monitored Wintermute's public market-making contract whitelists and BitGo's GitHub repository (Robinhood's custody provider) for advance notice of token listings.
For cashcat, a public BitGo pull request on July 27 and Wintermute's WETH pool approval on August 3 gave days of advance notice; the group accumulated over $1M at ~4% of supply.
When Robinhood listed three days later, the group realized $4M+ on cashcat, plus another $2M on a parallel PONS strategy.
The exploit required no privileged access, only structured monitoring of public contract approval events and custody repositories.

items.title: Security Breaches Accelerate Across the Crypto Ecosystem
points: Stablecoin supply fell from $303B to under $288B in 30 days (Oct 15–Nov 15), the steepest drop since June 2022, signaling broader market stress.
Arkham Intelligence traced $63M of the $387.5M Bitget hack to CoinJoin mixing transactions (a technique that obscures the source of funds by pooling multiple users' transactions together).
Initia suffered a second exploit in under three weeks (Nov 11), losing $3.27M.
October's incident cluster—PHP2Shell exposing 5M+ hosts, Railway decrypting secrets across 100K workspaces, Binance's $6.3B loss—shows AI has driven exploitation costs toward zero.
Three emerging threat vectors are agents as weapons, agents as targets, and agents as impostors, pushing expectations for decentralized reputation and agent-identity protocols in mainstream apps.
